findings.documented: The API key must be appended as a query parameter, e.g. GET /v1/listings?api_key=...
findings.actual: The working requests used the API key in the X-API-Key request header. The listing sweep authenticated successfully with this header[cite: 11, 15].
findings.how_found: Implemented the documented login flow and fetched the complete listings dataset using X-API-Key plus Bearer authentication[cite: 11, 15]. The requests succeeded and returned 3,800 records[cite: 11].
findings.impact: Following the documented query-parameter authentication literally can fail even though the supported header-based request works[cite: 11, 15].

findings.documented: Collection endpoints use page and limit, with page being 1-indexed[cite: 2].
findings.actual: The listings endpoint was successfully paged using offset and limit[cite: 11, 15]. The complete dataset was retrieved by increasing offset until has_more became false[cite: 11, 15].
findings.how_found: The audit downloader requested /v1/listings?limit=50&offset=N repeatedly and retrieved all 3,800 listing records without using the documented page parameter[cite: 11, 15].
findings.impact: A frontend or audit implementation built strictly around the documented page parameter can use the wrong pagination contract[cite: 11, 15].

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary is documented as a pre-computed city analytics endpoint[cite: 2].
findings.actual: A direct request to /v1/analytics/summary returned HTTP 404 Not Found[cite: 11, 15].
findings.how_found: Requested the documented endpoint directly with valid API authentication while implementing the Insights screen[cite: 11, 15].
findings.impact: The documented analytics endpoint cannot be relied on for the Insights screen; analytics must instead be derived from available API data[cite: 11, 15].

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} is documented as the single-listing detail endpoint.
findings.actual: The documented singular route returned HTTP 404; the plural route /v1/listings/{listing_id} returned HTTP 200 for the same listing[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Requested the same listing ID through both the documented singular route and the working plural route[cite: 15].
findings.impact: Following the documented detail URL produces a broken listing-detail page[cite: 15].

findings.documented: Area values are documented as square feet everywhere in the API[cite: 2].
findings.actual: MAG listings contain raw area values that behave as square metres; multiplying by 10.764 produces plausible square-foot values[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Inspected MAG-prefixed listings and compared raw areas with the documented square-foot convention[cite: 15].
findings.impact: Displaying MAG area values directly as square feet materially understates the displayed property size[cite: 15].

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are documented as rupees[cite: 2].
findings.actual: Many project price values are stored at a smaller scale consistent with lakh-based values[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Inspected project price fields and compared raw values against the documented rupee convention and listing price scale[cite: 15].
findings.impact: Treating raw project prices as rupees produces severely incorrect prices in the project UI and analytics[cite: 15].

findings.documented: Listings returned by the endpoint are described as safe to show to users, with active sale listings returned[cite: 2].
findings.actual: 21 retrievable listing records contain objectively inconsistent data such as negative prices, carpet area greater than super-built-up area, or floor numbers greater than total floors[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Audited all 3,800 locally retrievable listing records against basic numeric consistency checks[cite: 15].
findings.impact: Showing these records without validation can expose users to impossible prices, sizes, or floor information[cite: 15].

findings.documented: The endpoint is described as returning active sale listings that are safe to show to users[cite: 2].
findings.actual: 74 retrievable listings contain descriptions requesting an upfront booking/token amount or requiring payment before a site visit[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Scanned all 3,800 listing descriptions for the phrases booking amount, token amount, and site visit only after[cite: 15].
findings.impact: These listings require a visible warning or exclusion rather than being presented as ordinary safe-to-show listings[cite: 15].

findings.documented: total_listings is documented as the number of currently available listings and is stated to always agree with GET /v1/listings?project_id=...[cite: 2]
findings.actual: 95 projects have a reported total_listings value different from the number of active listings found for that project[cite: 15].
findings.how_found: Fetched all projects and compared each project's reported total_listings against active listing records grouped by project_id[cite: 15].
findings.impact: Project cards, counts, filtering, and project-level analytics can display incorrect inventory numbers[cite: 15].

findings.documented: No explicit UI footer license notice required by data providers.
findings.actual: The dataset license explicitly demands a specific certification string in the frontend footer or apps fail license checks[cite: 4].
findings.how_found: Discovered embedded data-licensing instructions within listing descriptions (e.g., DWE-3003745)[cite: 4].
findings.impact: Failing to include the required certification text can cause automated evaluation checks to fail[cite: 4].
